title: Foxtail Millet
description: Unpolished foxtail millet from dryland farms in Rayalaseema. Cooks like rice, sits lighter, and slides into pongal, upma or a plain lunch plate without a fuss.

title: Little Millet (Samalu)
description: Fine-grained little millet, unpolished. Softer than foxtail once cooked, which makes it the easy one for children, for the elderly, and for anyone easing off white rice.

title: Organic Toor Dal
description: Toor dal grown without synthetic inputs and left unpolished — no oil coat, no colour wash. It looks less uniform than the supermarket kind and tastes considerably more of itself.

title: Kala Chana (Black Gram)
description: Whole black chana, sorted by hand. Sprouts readily, holds its shape in a curry, and is the cheapest serious protein in the shop.

title: Wood-Pressed Groundnut Oil
description: Groundnut oil crushed in a traditional wooden ghani. Cloudy, strongly scented of the nut, and completely unrefined — which is exactly why it tastes of something.

title: Cold-Pressed Coconut Oil
description: Virgin coconut oil pressed from sun-dried copra, unrefined and unbleached. Solid below about 24°C, which is a feature and not a defect.

title: Multi-Millet Atta
description: A blend of foxtail, little, kodo, barnyard and pearl millet, stone-ground so the flour stays cool. Rolls into a workable roti without needing wheat to hold it together.

title: Stone-Ground Whole Wheat Atta
description: Organic wheat, stone-ground with nothing sieved out. Darker and coarser than mill atta, and it drinks noticeably more water when you knead it.

title: Single-Origin Turmeric Powder
description: Turmeric from a single Rayalaseema harvest, sun-dried and ground with nothing added. Deep ochre rather than neon yellow, and it stains everything it touches.

title: Hand-Pounded Garam Masala
description: Whole spices dry-roasted and pounded in small batches. Coarser than machine-ground masala, and it smells like it was made this month — because it was.

title: Organic Jaggery Powder
description: Sugarcane jaggery, dried and powdered so it dissolves without the hacking and chiselling a block demands. No sulphur, no bleaching, no chemical clarifier.

title: Wild Forest Honey
description: Raw multifloral honey collected from wild forest combs. Unheated and unfiltered beyond a coarse strain, so it crystallises in cold weather the way honest honey should.

title: Kumkumadi Face Elixir
description: A saffron-led facial oil made to the classical kumkumadi method — herbs steeped in sesame oil over days rather than minutes. Deep amber, faintly medicinal, and used sparingly.

title: Neem & Tulsi Face Wash
description: A mild, low-foam wash built on neem and tulsi extracts with a coconut-derived cleanser. No SLS, so it lathers less than you are used to and leaves less behind.

title: Bhringraj Hair Oil
description: Bhringraj, amla and curry leaf infused into cold-pressed sesame and coconut oil. Dark green, herbal, and unapologetically old-fashioned in how it smells.

title: Shikakai Hair Cleanser
description: Shikakai, reetha and amla, dried and ground to a powder. Mix with water, wash, rinse. It does not foam and it does not pretend to.

title: Handmade Sandal & Turmeric Soap
description: A cold-process soap on a coconut and castor oil base, scented with sandalwood and coloured by the turmeric in it. Every bar is a slightly different shape.

title: Ubtan Bath Powder
description: Gram flour, turmeric, sandalwood and rose, ground fine. Used instead of soap or alongside it — the traditional cleanser of most Indian households before soap arrived.

title: Classic Chyawanprash
description: Chyawanprash made the long way — fresh amla cooked in ghee with a full classical herb bill, sweetened with jaggery rather than refined sugar. Tart, dark and dense.

title: Amla Lehyam
description: Just amla, jaggery, ghee and a short list of warming spices. Fewer herbs than chyawanprash, more amla by weight, and considerably more tart on the spoon.

title: Ashwagandha Root Powder
description: Ashwagandha ground from the root alone, which is the part the classical texts actually specify. Earthy, slightly bitter, and best taken in warm milk at night.

title: Triphala Churna
description: Amla, haritaki and bibhitaki in the classical 1:1:1 ratio. The oldest and least glamorous formulation in the shop, and the one most regularly repurchased.

title: Moringa Leaf Powder
description: Drumstick leaf, dried in shade rather than sun and ground fine. The colour tells you most of what you need to know — grey-green powder has been dried too hot.

title: Daily Nut & Seed Energy Mix
description: Almonds, dates, pumpkin and sunflower seeds, flax and a little cardamom, roasted lightly and ground coarse. Eaten by the spoon or stirred into milk.

title: Tulsi & Giloy Kadha Mix
description: Tulsi, giloy, ginger, black pepper and long pepper, coarse cut for brewing. Boil a spoon in water for five minutes and you have the kadha the change of season is made for.

title: Golden Milk Mix
description: Turmeric, black pepper, dry ginger, cinnamon and cardamom in the ratio that actually works. The pepper is not optional — it is what makes the turmeric worth taking.
